title: Japanese Curry Chicken Potpie
ingredients: 1 1/4 cups chopped unpeeled Yukon gold potatoes (1/2-inch)
1 (3.2-oz) package mild Japanese curry mix, cubed (Golden Curry)
1/2 (17.3-oz) package frozen puff pastry, thawed - 1 sheet (Pepperidge Farm)
steps: Heat the oven to 400F. Heat the oil in a 10-inch cast iron skillet over medium until shimmering. Add onion, carrots and potatoes and cook, stirring frequently, until the carrots and potatoes just start to soften, 4-5 min.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 min.
Add the stock and bring to a boil over medium-high, stirring occasionally. Reduce to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are fork tender, 8-10 min.
Stir in the curry mix, ketchup and salt until dissolved and the mixture thickens, about 2 min. Stir in the chicken until evenly distributed. Remove from heat and keep warm.

Roll the pastry on a lightly floured surface into a 13-inch square. Lay it over the skillet and trim, leaving a 3/4- to 1-inch overhang. Fold the pastry under itself so the rolled edge is flush with the top of the skillet, then crimp into the side with a fork. It's fine if it doesn't adhere perfectly.
Brush the top with beaten egg and cut 8 slits (1 1/2-2 inches) to vent.
Bake until the pastry is golden brown and the filling is bubbly, about 30 min. Let stand 15 min before serving - this is not optional, it needs to set.
notes: Uses a store-bought Japanese curry roux block (Golden Curry, mild) from the international aisle - that's what makes the sauce silky and gravy-thick. Ketchup is the sweetness that makes it read as Japanese curry rather than generic. Rotisserie chicken keeps it a weeknight dish; skip the chicken for a vegetarian version. MAKE AHEAD: filling keeps 3 days in the fridge; loosen with a Tbsp or two of water and reheat gently over medium-low before topping. Bake the pastry fresh - it doesn't survive reheating crisp.

title: Red Curry Dumpling Soup
ingredients: 1/2 tsp thinly sliced red Thai chile, plus more to garnish
3 cups reduced-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
32 frozen mini wontons (pork, chicken or vegetable)
Garnish: cilantro, Thai basil, scallions, sliced red chile, crushed peanuts, lime wedges
steps: Heat oil in a large saucepan or medium Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown the mushrooms, stirring occasionally, 5-8 min.
Drop to medium. Add shallot, garlic, ginger, chile and salt; stir often until the shallots soften, 1-2 min.
Stir in the curry paste and cook, stirring constantly, until slightly darkened and very fragrant, about 1 min.
Add broth, coconut milk, fish sauce, lime juice and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium-high.

Add the wontons, return to a simmer, then stir in the bok choy. Reduce to medium and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the dumplings are cooked through and the bok choy is tender-crisp, 3-5 min.
Divide among bowls, garnish, and serve immediately.
notes: Swap spinach or napa cabbage for the bok choy; any frozen dumpling works. Chili oil drizzle for extra heat. Leftovers keep 2 days max - dumplings go mushy after that.

title: Lemony Miso Cabbage
ingredients: 1 lb green cabbage, chopped into 1-inch pieces, layers separated (about 6 cups)
steps: Whisk the miso with 1/4 cup water in a small bowl, mashing until it fully dissolves.
Melt the butter in a 12-inch nonstick skillet (one with a lid) over medium-high. Add the cabbage, season with salt and pepper, and stir to coat in the butter, about 1 min.
Drizzle the miso mixture over the top and stir it through. Cover and cook until the cabbage is just softened, about 2 min.

Uncover, mix well, then spread the cabbage into an even layer. Leave it undisturbed until the liquid has cooked off and the underside is lightly golden, about 2 min - this is where the sweetness comes from.
Turn off the heat. Add the lemon juice and dill and mix, scraping up any browned bits. Taste and season again with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a shallow bowl. Good warm or at room temperature.
notes: Butter + miso makes a silky savory sauce that carries the cabbage; the lemon and dill at the end cut the richness. Steam first, then caramelize - do not stir during the browning step or it just steams. Side dish for pan-roasted chicken, fish or steak, and good over rice or noodles. Five ingredients, one pan, about 15 minutes.

title: Quick Chicken Laksa
ingredients: 3-4 Tbsp shop-bought laksa paste (or red curry paste)
1/4 cucumber, cut into very thin matchsticks
steps: Boil a large saucepan of water. Cook the eggs 6 min, then drop them into cold water and leave until needed.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium-high. Fry the laksa paste 2-3 min, until the oil turns reddish - that colour change is the cue it has bloomed.
Stir in the chicken stock, coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar. Cover and bring to the boil.
Add the chicken breast, re-cover, drop to medium and cook 10-12 min, until cooked through.
Meanwhile put the vermicelli in a large heatproof bowl, pour over 1 litre of just-boiled water to cover, and leave to soak while the chicken cooks. Drain just before serving.
Lift the chicken out to a plate and keep the soup warm over low heat. Let the chicken cool enough to handle, then shred it into chunks with forks or your hands.
Divide the drained noodles between two bowls, top with the shredded chicken, and ladle over enough soup to just cover the noodles.
Peel and halve the eggs and add to the bowls. Garnish with cucumber, mint, coriander and chilli; serve with lime wedges.
notes: From the BBC Food reel (@bbcfood) - Justin Tsang's shortcut on a dish that traditionally takes hours. The shop-bought paste is doing the heavy lifting, so the brand matters: laksa paste is the real thing, red curry paste is the fallback. 6-minute eggs give a jammy yolk; add a minute if you want them firmer. Pour the soup over the noodles only to cover - drowning them makes it watery. About 900 kcal per serving as written; use light coconut milk to cut it back.

title: Thai Green Curry Lentil Soup (One Pot, Dry Lentils)
source: Food & Wine, adapted for dry pardina lentils
ingredients: 1 (4-oz) package sliced mixed mushrooms (cremini, oyster, shiitake)
1 (1-inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped (about 2 Tbsp)
2 large garlic cloves, finely chopped (about 1 Tbsp)
1 bunch scallions, dark greens separated from white and light green, thinly sliced
1/4 cup green curry paste (Maesri or similar)
2/3 cup dry pardina lentils, rinsed and picked over
2 cups peeled butternut squash, 1/2-inch chop (about 12 oz)
1 bunch fresh cilantro with tender stems, coarsely chopped, plus more to garnish
1 tsp fish sauce (Red Boat or similar)
3/4 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
Thinly sliced Fresno chile, to garnish
steps: Heat the oil in a medium Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave them alone until browned on one side, 3-4 min. Stir and keep cooking until tender, about 2 min more.

Add the ginger, garlic, and the white and light green scallion, stirring constantly until fragrant, about 1 min. Stir in the curry paste and cook, stirring, 1 min more - blooming it in the oil is what deepens the broth.
Add the broth and the rinsed lentils. Bring to a boil, then drop to medium-low, cover, and simmer 10 min. The lentils get a head start because they need roughly twice as long as the squash.

Add the squash, re-cover, and simmer 12-15 min more, until the squash is tender and the lentils are tender but still holding their shape. Start checking at 10 min - pardina go from firm to mushy quickly. If it looks tight, splash in more broth.
While it simmers: set aside 1/4 cup of the coconut milk for drizzling. Put the rest in a blender with the cilantro, miso and scallion greens. Blend smooth, about 30 seconds.
Stir in the fish sauce, salt, and the blended coconut mixture. Cook over medium, stirring often, just until warmed through, about 2 min - no longer, or the green fades.
Taste for salt. Dry lentils drink up seasoning as they cook, so this usually needs more salt than you would expect.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with the reserved coconut milk, and top with Fresno chile and more cilantro. Lime wedges at the table.
notes: ONE POT, DRY LENTILS - this is the default version. 2/3 cup dry pardina replaces the 8-oz pouch of pre-cooked black lentils in the original. Broth is up from 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 cups because the lentils absorb it; top up with more if it tightens. The two timers that matter: lentils 22-25 min total, squash 12-15 min, which is why the lentils go in first. IF USING PRE-COOKED POUCH LENTILS instead: use 1 1/2 cups broth, add the squash with the broth and simmer 10-12 min, then stir the pouch lentils in at step 6 - about 30 min total. Other dry lentils: French green or beluga behave the same. Brown or green work but go softer, check earlier. Skip red lentils, they dissolve. Frozen butternut is fine straight from frozen; it softens faster and releases water, so start checking early. Mushrooms: spread them out and do not stir for the first few minutes or they steam instead of browning. Green curry pastes vary a lot in heat and salt - taste before the final seasoning. Vegetarian: use vegetable broth and skip the fish sauce (add a little extra miso or salt). Serve as-is, or over steamed jasmine rice for a bigger dinner.
